weather_line: Overcast in the hollows · the drive is quiet · forty-seven degrees between ducks

stories.headline: A Note Has Been Left: Folded Beneath the Orange Duck's Base, Four Words, the Same Ink as the Stamp
stories.byline: By our Drive Correspondent, filing from the front steps
body: At six forty-one this morning, Steve discovered a folded square of paper tucked beneath the base of the orange duck on the passenger-side mirror. The fold was precise — four corners meeting, sealed with what the Prophet's investigative desk has confirmed is the same burnt-sienna ink used to stamp the numeral 7 beneath the duck's left wing. The two ducks remained at forty-seven degrees. Nothing else had been touched.

The note contains four words. The Prophet has obtained their text. They read: 'Survey 7. You know.' This office declines to speculate further in print, except to note the following: survey marker 7 sits forty yards below Christine's crossing line on the Harlan's Creek tributary grid; the note is not signed; and Lucy, when shown the paper, turned away at once and went to her bed, which investigators describe as 'the most informative thing she has ever done.'

stories.headline: Friday Arrives Briskly; Is Immediately Organised; the Week Ends Better Than It Began and Christine Is Why
body: By nine o'clock this morning, three outstanding accounts had been reconciled, one goblin dispute had been reclassified as 'a misunderstanding stemming from arithmetic,' and a vault access backlog that had quietly accumulated since Tuesday had been cleared without ceremony. Griphook the Younger, asked to comment, said only: 'The week held.' He has been writing that phrase on a card and keeping it in his desk. It is not yet clear what he plans to do with it.
The Senior Client Liaison departed at five past seventeen. The ledgers, sources confirm, were already balanced. They are not always balanced when she leaves. They are always balanced when she leaves.

stories.headline: Subcommittee Receives Text of Note; Reads It Three Times; Determines That 'You Know' May Constitute a Second Jurisdiction; Drafts Memo Accordingly
body: The Ministry's Duck and Pavement Markings Subcommittee convened at eleven this morning upon receipt of the note's transcription, forwarded by this office as a professional courtesy. The chair read the note aloud twice. A member read it a third time silently. A motion was tabled to claim jurisdiction over the phrase 'you know' on the grounds that it implies institutional knowledge the Subcommittee does not yet possess but would very much like to.

The motion passed four to one. The dissenting member noted that jurisdiction over an implication is 'philosophically fraught.' The chair acknowledged this and asked that it be recorded. It has been recorded. The Subcommittee adjourns at three and reconvenes tomorrow, with or without answers.

stories.headline: The Weekend Stands Ready; Steve Has Already Checked the Winch; the Kitchen Table Still Has the Flint Stone on It; Everything Is in Its Place
body: As of this evening, the enchanted Jeep is trail-ready, the flint from Keeps Ridge sits at the head of the kitchen table exactly where it was placed on Sunday, and the chart remains folded at the new mark. Steve, asked about weekend plans, said he had 'a few ideas' and consulted the margin of something. The Jeep, when queried directly, did not respond but did appear to lean slightly forward.

Christine, completing the week's final report from the armchair where the best reports are always written, declined to confirm or deny any forthcoming expedition. The ducks, for their part, held their forty-seven-degree angle through the evening and have not moved. The drive is quiet. Someone, however, has been on it. The weekend begins.

familiars_corner: Lucy: turned away from the note this morning before Steve had fully unfolded it, returned to her bed, and has not moved in four hours. No statement has been issued. A statement is being drafted.

Ellie: examined the note carefully, determined it was not a biscuit, and asked if anyone else wanted to go outside. No one did. She went anyway and reported back that the drive smelled 'like Thursday, but more so.'

Jersey: observed all of the above from the warmest chair in the front room, found none of it relevant to his immediate requirements, and requested that someone come and sit with him. Steve sat with him for eleven minutes, which Jersey logged as 'satisfactory.'
founding_editor_note: Four words on a folded note is a solid structure. I built a staircase once on less information than that, and it's still standing. — D.

in_brief.sport: The Prophet's Strongwitch Correspondent notes that Friday is heavier than Thursday and Christine lifted it without visible effort.
in_brief.forecast: Overcast through the weekend, with a strong possibility of answers by Sunday and a forty percent chance of mud.

storyline_updates.title: The Duck Waits
storyline_updates.summary: Day 4: A folded note in burnt-sienna ink — the same as the stamp on the orange duck — has been found beneath the duck's base. Text: 'Survey 7. You know.' Lucy turned away from it immediately and retreated to her bed, confirming prior knowledge of the Bandit. The two ducks remain at forty-seven degrees. Day 5 — the final day — should resolve the arc: the Bandit's identity revealed (a trail figure known to Christine and Steve, someone who was at Harlan's Creek the morning of the expedition — a fellow off-roader, a trail-keeping volunteer, or someone connected to the survey markers), Lucy's collusion explained (she met this person on the drive at some earlier point and approved of them), and the forty-seven-degree angle given its final meaning. The resolution should be warm and funny, not sinister — the Bandit is an admirer of the line Christine ran, leaving a small tribute. A third duck, or the return of something from the ridge, may mark the conclusion.
